title: Echoes of Exploration: The Signal Archive

opening.title: The Quiet Observatory
curator_rules: Memory echoes are dramatizations reconstructed from historical records.
Evidence panels contain sourced, peer-reviewed NASA facts and instruments.
A good Archivist separates what happened, what scientists inferred, and what the story imagines.
opening.intro_copy: The Observatory of Echoes stands quiet on the edge of night. Thirty-one records of distant explorers rest in the archive, waiting for their signals to be traced back to the questions that launched them. Reconstruct nine featured echoes across the Moon, Mars, and Elsewhere to restore the observatory wings.

ending.title: The Archive Is Alive When It Is Used
ending.summary: All nine echoes now stand beside their instruments, measurements, and primary NASA sources. The hardware on the Moon, Mars, 433 Eros, and interstellar space did not awaken—our understanding of how engineering turns questions into evidence did.
ending.closing_line: A mission ends. Its evidence keeps traveling.

chapters.title: Chapter I — Moon: Learning to Reach
chapters.theme: Before distant science, machines had to land softly, measure precisely, and move across unfamiliar terrain.

discovery_bridge.title: Discovery Bridge I: From Soft Touchdown to Field Geology
discovery_bridge.summary: Surveyor 1 proved a spacecraft could touch lunar soil softly without sinking. That confidence allowed Apollo 11 to land crews and leave passive laser reflectors that still measure Earth–Moon distance today—and by Apollo 17, the Lunar Roving Vehicle turned a pinpoint landing into 30+ km of field geology across Taurus–Littrow.

chapters.title: Chapter II — Mars: Reading a Changing World
chapters.theme: Instruments turn rocks, soil, thin air, wheel tracks, and unexpected setbacks into clues about a planet's history.

discovery_bridge.title: Discovery Bridge II: Soil Chemistry to Aerial Scouting
discovery_bridge.summary: Viking 1 taught scientists that searching for life requires careful multiple-test reasoning rather than hasty conclusions. Decades later, Spirit's stuck wheel accidentally scraped up silica-rich clues of ancient water, while Ingenuity proved rotorcraft can scout Martian terrain through air 1% as dense as Earth's.

chapters.title: Chapter III — Elsewhere: Beyond the Familiar
chapters.theme: Extreme distance changes everything—power budgets, antenna pointing, storage, timing, and adaptive engineering.

discovery_bridge.title: Discovery Bridge III: Adaptive Engineering at the Edge of the Solar System
discovery_bridge.summary: NEAR Shoemaker turned an asteroid orbiter into an unplanned surface probe on 433 Eros. Voyager 1 trades declining plutonium power to send back interstellar particle measurements via the Deep Space Network, while New Horizons compressed years of planning into a few fast hours at Pluto and Arrokoth.
